title.narrative: Output 6.4. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative:
1. In May 2023, the Government of Malawi adopted a newly revised workplace labour inspection tool as a measure to ensure equal opportunities and treatment of persons living with HIV and AIDS in the workplace. The newly revised inspection tool is aligned to international commitments such as the ILO Conventions 155, 184 and 190, ILO Code of Practice on HIV and AIDS and the World of Work of 2001; the ILO Recommendation concerning HIV and AIDS and the World of Work (No.200) of 2010; and Sustainable Development Goal No. 3 on promoting healthy lives through equal treatment and non-discrimination of workers. In the final analysis, the inspection tool is contributing towards achieving the effective protection of workers and aim to achieve social justice and decent work for all. The tool is being utilized by Labour Inspectors and OSH inspectors in all the 28 districts of Malawi when conducting workplace inspections to ensure employers comply with provisions set in the HIV and AIDS Prevention Act for prohibition of discrimination in employment based on HIV status.
2. In July 2023, the Government of Malawi operationalized the Disability Inclusion Academy as a measure to ensure equal opportunities and treatment of persons with Disabilities. In 2022 the government of the Malawi and the Organisation of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) established the first-ever disability inclusion academy where 20 Disability Inclusion Facilitators (DIFs) champions were rigorously selected and trained to provide technical services and trainings to the government of Malawi rural development programmes which are being funded by IFAD in the four districts of Chitipa, Nkhata Bay, Thyolo and Kasungu. The DIFs also mobilised fellow persons with disabilities to find employment in government interventions. With support from the ILOIDS country envelopes project – Accelerating progress on HIV and AIDS and ending inequalities in the world of work in November 2022 convened a stakeholders’ meeting to discuss the revision of the workplace inspection tool to include real or perceived HIV status for People living with HIV in Malawi. The ILO provided feedback and comments in the meeting that adopted the revised inspection tool as a means of ensuring the protection of all the workers against discrimination based on real or perceived HIV status for PLHIV in the workplace. The final inspection checklist undertook a normative revision based on the proposed changes by the ILO. The approved inspection checklist approved by the Government of Malawi incorporates changes based on the ILO proposals. 2. With support from the NGO Light for the World, ILO convened a disability academy in December 2022 and provided training for Organisation of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and Government in the Disability Inclusion Facilitators (DIF) model through a Learning Route in Uganda. The ILO made presentations and led the discussions during the training sessions. Further, the ILO led the development of the curriculum for the academy which is currently being implemented by the Government of Malawi.

description.narrative: In 2023, the Government of Malawi approved an Occupational Health and Safety policy. This is in order to prevent and reduce the number of occupational accidents and injury to health, arising out of and/or linked with or occurring in the course of work, by minimising occupational risks or eliminating risks at the source, which promotes principles on risk management and developing a preventive safety and health culture that includes information, consultation and training. Through stakeholders’ consultation and social dialogue, the policy was developed in a comprehensive and gender-responsive national OSH Policy and programme. The Policy highlighted the phenomena of climate change including the increased magnitude and frequency of floods, droughts, strong winds and outbreaks of pests and diseases in Malawi, and anticipated negative impacts on the safety and health of workers. OSH policy and programme will ensure that workplace safety and health programmes are responsive to climate change by increasing awareness about impact of climate change on workplace safety and health and adapting work practices to minimise the impact of climate change on workplace safety and health. The national OSH programme targets to have at least two economic sectors having developed guidance for measures to mitigate impact of climate change in workplaces. In June 2022, the ILO compiled the national Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) profile for Malawi, drafted a gender-responsive national OSH Policy and held national seminars to raise awareness among key stakeholders regarding the ILO conventions on OSH. The ILO also collaborated with the Ministry of Health in the development of the OSH profile which informed the development of the Policy. The findings of the national OSH profile also pointed to natural disaster as one of major threats on Malawi’s national OSH interventions. In January 2023, the ILO provided normative feedback on the policy during a stakeholders’ meeting held in Malawi which have since been incorporated in the final policy document approved by the Government.

description.narrative: It has been confirmed that the upcoming Labour Force Survey will include the Washington Group/ILO disability module. This will allow not only to have the labour market data, including on informal employment, disaggregated by disability status but also highlight some of the root causes underlying the labour market participation of persons with disabilities The ILO Pretoria office and ILO HQ have not only been advocating for the inclusion of this module but also provided assistance to the Malawi National Statistical Office on how best to include this module. Furthermore, funds have been provided from the DC project “Sparking Disability Inclusive Rural Transformation” to cover the additional costs linked to the inclusion of this module in the survey.
